fix.notes: The alias approach is additive — it only appends the canonical zone when it isn't already in the current-abbreviation matches, so no existing results are removed. MST/HST (Arizona, Hawaii — no DST) will always appear via the normal match path anyway, so CANONICAL_TZ_ALIASES for those is a harmless belt-and-suspenders addition.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`/time EST` showed Jamaica (America/Jamaica) but not New York because `times_from_timezone_code` matched timezones by their *current* abbreviation. America/New_York uses `EDT` in summer, so it only appeared when EST was the current abbreviation — Jamaica uses EST year-round with no DST, so it always matched.

## What changed

Added `CANONICAL_TZ_ALIASES` dict in `magic/fetcher.py` mapping common US abbreviations (`EST`, `EDT`, `CST`, `CDT`, `MST`, `MDT`, `PST`, `PDT`, `AKST`, `AKDT`, `HST`) to their canonical IANA timezone. `times_from_timezone_code()` now appends the canonical zone for any recognized alias before the match loop, so `EST` always includes `America/New_York` in results alongside any other current matches.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen pytest magic/fetcher_test.py -v` — 13 passed (4 pre-existing, 9 new regression tests covering all major US aliases and the specific EST→New York case)

Fixes #11645
